findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the front handwashing sink was without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. CORRECTED: PIC stated that new paper towels were available, but the key to open the dispenser had not yet been located, and instead they were using paper towels from the other handwashing sink in the other room. PIC located the key and replaced the paper towels during the inspection. Ensure that EACH handwashing sink is provided with disposable towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed 2 containers of house made pepper ranch in the prep cooler and the front 2-door cooler that had date marks for August, well beyond the 7 day period for discarding TCS foods. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded the items. Ensure that TCS, RTE foods are discarded within 7 days, with day 1 being date of preparation or opening, and day 7 being date of final use or discard.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Notified PIC that the area needs to be cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil residues. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that there was duct tape on the handle of the back 2-door (egg) cooler. Duct tape is not an approved repair, because it is not smooth and easily cleanable. Eliminate duct tape and repair door handle with materials that are smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee moving from washing dirty dishes to donning gloves to begin food prep without washing hands between tasks. CORRECTED: Inspectors discussed handwashing and glove use procedures with PIC and Staff, including education on how hands should always be washed between tasks, and new gloves used for different tasks. Hands can quickly accumulate debris and microorganisms, which is why they should be cleaned frequently, especially as some contamination may not always be visible or noticeable. Ensure that all staff wash hands before putting on new gloves between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw hamburger patties being stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods like cheese in the front prep cooler bottom area. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and moved the raw hamburger patties below the RTE foods. Ensure that RTE foods are stored above raw foods, including raw meat.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer buckets (quaternary ammonium) were at concentrations too low for effective sanitizing (50 ppm). CORRECTED: PIC went to the source of the sanitizer (the hose for the triple sink sanitizing compartment) and realized that its container of sanitizer was empty. PIC promptly replaced the container and refilled the sanitizer buckets, which then measured at effective concentrations (200-400ppm). Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are measured frequently throughout service to confirm sanitizing effectiveness.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following equipment was observed in need of repair:
(i) Leaks were observed inside of two freezers (front 1-door and back 2-door), and the back 2-door (egg) cooler. Facility is taking additional measures in the meantime to prevent leaks from contaminating food. 
(ii) A leak was observed from the bottom of the steam table, resulting in water collecting on the floor of the cookline/service line. 
(iii) Duct tape on the back 2-door (egg) cooler is not an approved repair. Eliminate duct tape and repair door handle with materials that are smooth and easily cleanable.
Maintain equipment in good repair. Fix leaks to prevent water ponding on floors and inside coolers.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that staff Food Handler certificates were not available in the facility, and certificates were not provided to the Inspector electronically. Ensure that all food handlers employed at the facility have Food Handler certificates which are available upon request.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed the following foods lacking proper date marking: (1) The salads in the display cooler that were prepared yesterday; (2) The package of cut ham in the front double cooler that was opened yesterday; and (3) Container of cut tomatoes in the front double cooler that were prepared yesterday. The salads, cut ham, and cut tomatoes were properly date marked during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed that several foods were not date marked. Foods missing date marks includes, but is not limited too, boiled eggs, spinach, packaged chicken salad, ham, cut vegetables (such as tomatoes, onions, peppers, and lettuce), and various deli meats. The foods were date marked during the inspection. Ensure that food being held in the establishment for longer than 24 hours are date marked to clearly indicate the 7-day maximum. The day the food is prepared is day 1. The food must be discarded after 7 days. The facility was provided with an informational handout during the inspection. Ensure that foods are properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
It was observed that labels still have not been put on the cookies. The violation was observed during the 06/20/2024 inspection and the 07/09/2024 re-inspect. It was observed during the re-inspect today (07/19/2024) that labels still have not been put on the cookies. When inspectors arrived employees were in the process of labeling the peanut butter cookies, but they did not have labels for the remaining cookies. Cookies packaged in advance of retail sale in the food establishment must have proper labels or information available at point of sale. This includes ingredients list and allergen information. Provide required information for cookies either in label form or placard form. There will be a follow-up on 07/30/2024 to ensure that the cookies have been labeled. 

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled.

findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION. 

Inspector observed improper hand washing procedure during the inspection today. Employee was observed to wash hands but then fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure that all employees are aware of proper procedure for hand washing. Operator had a discussion with employee to ensure future compliance. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed poor hand washing practices occurring throughout the facility in multiple instances:
- Observed a food employee switch activities repeatedly and over a 15 minute period of time did not wash her hands at all. Activities included opening/closing the upright freezers, cooking food from frozen on the grill and fryers, and working with ready-to-eat food. Operator was instructed by person in charge to stop and wash hands but responded to the operator by saying she will but she was going to get chicken dropped into the fryer first. Manager failed to stop the action at this point and make corrections. Inspector stepped in and had food employee toss the chicken that had been pulled out of the freezer against managements instructions, strip the gloves, and wash her hands prior to returning to working with food. Education was provided to both operator and manager regarding proper hand washing frequencies. Education was provided to manager regarding the benefits of getting a CFM certification regarding managerial control and understanding of food safety practices. Inspector discussed with operator the need to establish and maintain managerial control regarding hand washing and other activities in the facility. Operator stated understanding of the reasons for hand washing between activity changes. Manager expressed understanding of the need for managerial control.
- Inspector observed a newer employee at the facility washing hands without using a barrier. Manager stopped the action and was able to successfully correct the behavior on site.
- Observed a newer employee wash hands in the middle basin of the triple sink. Manager was able to stop, educate and correct the action.

A follow-up is schedule for 9/29/2022 to ensure hand-washing procedure and frequency is corrected.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several priority/priority foundation violations throughout the course of inspection. Per discussion with PIC, the facility was short staffed due to a call-off today and there were two people working. Inspection was performed during a busy lunch period. Person in charge is not a certified food manager and was not aware of the differences between food handler and food manager certificates. Current person in charge does not have a food handler certificate or CFM. 

Managerial knowledge and control in the facility is lacking. Ensure that PIC is a certified food manager. Ensure that hand washing is occurring throughout the facility and take corrective actions based on healthy practices and 2017 FDA Food Code requirements. Work with building maintenance to ensure that required maintenance items are completed by next routine inspection. Monitor temperatures throughout the facility regularly. 

A 30-day follow-up is being issued to determine progress towards successful correction of the violations observed today and ensure that person in charge is effectively implementing corrective actions in the facility. 



The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf  

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed operator at the facility switching several activities while wearing gloves but without any hand washing. Operator grabbed the handle of the freezer, took food out of the freezer, used the gloved hand to put frozen breaded chicken and French fries in the fryer, proceed to grab an in-use spatula to cook on the grill, and then prepare ready to eat sandwiches all with the same gloves. Inspector had a conversation with PIC regarding hand washing in the facility and the need to wash hands any time contamination may occur. Ensure that gloves are changed between activities, especially those where employees are switching between frozen food to ready-eat-food without any kill step in between. Be observant to operational errors and ensure that if contamination is possible, employees immediately switch gloves and wash hands to prevent the contamination of food served to the public. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:

Upon inspector arrival, both hand sinks (on prep line and next to 3-part sink) observed without soap. Inspector asked staff to locate hand soap prior to continuing lunch service. Education provided. Hand soap and disposable towels must be available and stocked at hand sinks at all times. Changing of tasks and/or changing gloves requires a hand wash. If handwashing supplies run out, a staff member must be designated to replace supplies immediately.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

Containers of food in stainless steel cooler next to dry storage observed to be exceeding 7-day date mark including: 2 containers of gravy (7/12). Food voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. Education provided. The date of prep for food counts as day 1, therefore these foods expired yesterday 7/18. 

Additionally, a whole deli turkey observed with a mark of 7/7 in black ink. PIC advised the turkey had been pulled from frozen on 7/16. Inspector advised foods that are pulled from frozen should bear a new date mark so staff knows it had been frozen previously. PIC provided a new date label of 7/16 in red ink to indicate the new "day 1" of the product.
